excerpt: Weavable gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other agents one MCP endpoint with scoped, current context from 20+ work tools. $20/month after 30 days free.
content:
Weavable is a context layer that sits between a team's work tools and its AI assistants. You connect tools such as Jira, GitHub, Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot and Zendesk through one OAuth flow, choose which projects, channels and pipelines belong to a given workflow, and Weavable builds a graph that links tickets, threads and deals by account, team and timeline. That context is then exposed through a single MCP endpoint you can plug into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or your own agents.

The pitch is that direct tool connections hand the model raw data and let it guess what matters on every run. Weavable instead keeps a running changelog of what changed across your stack, scopes and ranks it before the model sees it, and keeps excluded areas (it gives HR and finance as examples) out of reach. Access is read-only, the company says data is never used for training, and it claims SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certification. It also offers an audit trail, a REST API and SSO.

Weavable is made by Thatworks.xyz Inc. (That Works), which gives a Delaware postal address in its terms. Its makers on Product Hunt are co-founders Abesh Thakur and Varun Nair, both of whom list past roles at Meta. It launched on Product Hunt on 11 May 2026, hunted by Ben Lang, and finished #6 for the day with 228 upvotes and 65 comments. Individual use is free for 30 days and then $20 a month; team and custom plans are by contact.

We have not tested Weavable ourselves. This page brings together its official site, documentation and legal pages, its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

quotes.text: How does Weavable handle permissions and context boundaries so agents only reason from the information that specific users or teams should ... see?
quotes.reply: Source connections are read-only and tightly scoped OAuth, and agents never connect to data sources directly, only to contexts you have defined with explicit data scopes.
quotes.author: Conor McKenna

quotes.text: Curious: how do you actually reduce token usage by 90%?
quotes.reply: Pulling raw data costs twice, on ingestion and again while the model connects records; Weavable's graph already knows the relationships and recency, so the model reasons only over the signals it queries.
quotes.author: Grant MacLennan

faq.a: A context layer for AI agents. It connects your work tools, builds a linked, scoped view of what is happening across them, and serves it through one MCP endpoint for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or your own agents.
The Individual plan is free for 30 days and then $20 a month. Teams (up to 25 seats included) and Custom plans are priced on request.

faq.q: Why not connect my tools to Claude or ChatGPT directly?
faq.a: You can. Weavable's argument is that direct connections return raw data and the model decides what matters differently each time, while Weavable pre-builds the relationships, tracks changes and limits what reaches the model.

faq.q: Can Weavable change data in my tools?
faq.a: No. The company says it uses read-only OAuth and cannot write to any connected tool.

faq.q: Is my data used to train AI models?
faq.a: Weavable says your data is not shared, not retained and not used to train any model, and that it holds SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certification with the report available on request.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Weavable?
faq.a: Composio for giving agents tool access, or Glean for enterprise AI search. Weavable sits between the two as a read-only context endpoint.

paragraphs: Abesh Thakur, co-founder of That Works, says teams building agent workflows already hold the context they need (decisions, relationships, pipeline data and support history), but it is spread across every tool. Connecting apps directly floods the model with raw responses and burns tokens, while static knowledge bases and RAG go stale as soon as they are captured.

Weavable keeps a continuously updated changelog across a team's work tools so agents reason from current, connected context. He claimed one-tenth the tokens of direct app connections and outputs preferred 85% of the time in LLM-as-a-judge evaluations; these are the company's own figures.
launch_story.attribution: Abesh Thakur, maker, on Product Hunt

liked: Treating context as something that changes, through an activity graph and changelog
Capturing what caused a change, which commenters felt plain RAG misses

How permissions and sensitive data are handled (read-only OAuth, and agents only reach contexts you define)
Whether it is faster than connecting Claude Code to each data source (yes, the makers say, because retrieval work is done upstream)
Whether context is normalised before it reaches different models (it is ranked, de-noised and structured first)
